conclusion: Organic branch topology and independent output layers use different Z grids: clip output slices and propagated roots using belt-floor polygons evaluated at each output layer's physical print_z, not the topology cache index, and keep a positive regular height for negative-Z layer zero. Parallel overhang sampling can emit tips and roofs onto shared lower layers; quantized tip deduplication must publish layer-local candidates in stable source-layer order rather than mutex acquisition order. Otherwise even fresh slices with identical settings can generate different support geometry, and support-only re-slices differ from a fresh slice.
